title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from p.87). X_n is a Riemann sphere obtained from a regular 2n-gon P, called a 'polygon' with its flags. The dihedral group D_n of order 2n acts holomorphically on it. The quotient map g_n: X_n -> X_0 = P^1(C) is a Belyi-type map branched over 0, 1, ∞. The fibres are as follows.
- Over ∞: the two poles P_ω, P_ω', with stabiliser of order n.
- Over 1: the n points Q_a, with stabiliser of order 2.
- Over 0: the points R_a, which are removed.
So X_n^* = X_n minus the orbit over 0. The quotient orbifold is X_0^* = X_0 \ {0} with signature 2{1} + n{∞}, and 0 is treated as a cusp (multiplicity ∞). Its orbifold fundamental group is Π_{0,3}/<ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n>, which is isomorphic to Z/2 * Z/n.

On the previous page Grothendieck had only exterior (outer) isomorphisms (93). The barycentric subdivision of X_0 has the two hemispheres X_0^± as faces. Pulling it back gives 4n triangles on X_n, of which 2n are 'direct'. He fixes an origin flag r_0 = (R_0, Q_{a0}, P_ω), mapped holomorphically onto X_0^+. He takes as base point the point P in r_0 above the 'north pole' P_+ = exp(2iπ/6) of X_0^+. That point is the barycentre of the upper triangle, the fixed point of the order-3 symmetry of P^1 \ {0,1,∞}.

On this page:
(95) Equivariant theory gives a genuine (not merely outer) isomorphism Π_1(X_n^*, D_n; P) ≅ Π_1(X_0^*, 2{1}+n{∞}; P_+) ≅ Π_{0,3}/<ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n>. Here Π_1(X, G; P) is the equivariant fundamental group, i.e. π_1 of the quotient stack [X/G]. Its elements are pairs (ℓ, g) with g ∈ D_n and ℓ a path g(P) -> P. The map is the obvious one, (ℓ, g) |-> g_n(ℓ), which is a loop at P_+ = g_n(P). One may take ℓ inside X_n^{**} = X_n minus the ramification points = g_n^{-1}(U_{0,3}). Its class in the quotient of Π_{0,3} depends only on the class of (ℓ, g).
(96) To make the earlier (93) precise, compose with a base-point change Π_1(X_n^*, D_n; P_{n+}) -> Π_1(X_n^*, D_n; P). This uses the unique homotopy class of a path α inside the origin flag r_0, as in the figure.
(97) The composite g_n: Π_1(X_n^*, D_n; P_+) -> Π_1(X_0, ∞{0}+2{1}+n{∞}; P_+) ≅ Π_{0,3}/<ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n>. He then begins evaluating it on the generators ρ (rotation of order n about the poles) and σ_{a0} (half-turn about Q_{a0}).

The image of ρ under (96) is represented by a path α_ρ: ρ(P) -> P in X_n^{**}, obtained by deforming α·ρ(α)^{-1}. The method is to count crossings of α_ρ with the 1-skeleton of the barycentric subdivision. The equator arcs (∞,0), (0,1), (1,∞) of X_0 lift to edges, so the crossing sequence of the projected loop at P_+ determines its class in Π_{0,3}; this is a cutting-sequence argument. The next page completes the computation: g_n(ρ) = ρ_∞^{-1} and g_n(σ_{a0}) = ρ_1 (= ρ_1^{-1}).

Purpose: to obtain explicit, base-pointed identifications of the dihedral 'polygon' groups with quotients of Π_{0,3}. These are needed in the Teichmüller / dessin programme of 1981–82, where one compares the action of Gal(Q̄/Q) or of mapping classes on Π_{0,3} with symmetries of regular polygons.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. Notation is loose: P_+ is used for the base point upstairs (P_{n+} of p.87) as well as for exp(2iπ/6) in X_0. In ℓ: g(P_*) -> P_*, the base point should be P.
On the next page the quotient is written Π_{0,3}/<ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^2>. In context it should be ρ_∞^n; the argument only uses ρ_1^2 = 1.
X_n^{**} written as 'X_n | U_{03}' should read g_n^{-1}(U_{0,3}) (or X_n minus the ramification points), as the preceding lines say.

ideas.what: Equivariant fundamental group Π_1(X, G; P) of pairs (ℓ, g), and its isomorphism with the orbifold fundamental group of the quotient with signature (here 2{1} + n{∞} + ∞{0})
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group of the quotient stack / orbifold fundamental group; Z/2 * Z/n as a quotient of Π_{0,3}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) alludes to fundamental groups 'à multiplicités/signatures'; SGA1 has related tame/equivariant material

ideas.what: Choosing the barycentre exp(iπ/3) of the upper half-plane triangle as an honest base point, and the origin flag r_0 to rigidify outer isomorphisms into actual isomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: base-point rigidification (cf. tangential base points, Deligne 1989)

ideas.what: Computing classes in Π_{0,3} by counting crossings of lifted paths with the edges of the barycentric subdivision (the equator arcs)
ideas.modern_name: cutting sequences / combinatorial computation of monodromy of a dessin

ideas.what: Regular polygon / dihedral sphere X_n -> P^1 as a Galois Belyi map with group D_n, and explicit images of the generators ρ and σ_a in Π_{0,3}/<ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n>
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses regular polyhedra/polygons as dessins in general terms

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but routine bookkeeping: base-pointed identification of a dihedral orbifold fundamental group with Z/2 * Z/n inside Π_{0,3}, computed by cutting sequences. It is standard material, interesting only as a window on Grothendieck's working method in the Teichmüller notes.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'La théorie équivariante donne un iso (pas extérieur !)'. This means not merely an outer isomorphism, in contrast with (93) on the previous page.
'provenant d'un chemin α dessus [?], comme dans le plan [?]' likely reads 'provenant d'un chemin α dans r_0 (underlined), comme dans la figure'. The path α lies in the origin flag r_0.
'L'homomorphisme naturel, ce qui précise (95), quand ! Puis, est donné' should read 'L'homomorphisme naturel, qui précise (95), quant à lui, est donné par la formule des plus évidentes'.
'un lacet dans P_+ = g_n(P)' should read 'un lacet en P_+ = g_n(P)'.
'ℓ : g(P_*) -> P_*' should be ℓ : g(P) -> P, with g_n(ℓ): g_n(P) -> g_n(P).
(97): the struck-out label is 'g'; the replacement is 'g_n'.
'ρ(P_*) --α_ρ--> P_3 [?]' should be 'ρ(P) --α_ρ--> P' (an overwritten P).
Margin NB: 'α_ρ est obtenu par déformation dans X_n^{**} des chemins composés α ρ(α)^{-1}'.
